heading: Outside, and ready for winter.
lede: Siding, trim, porches, and shutters. We wash, scrape, and prime first, and we keep an eye on the weather.
includesHeading: The whole outside of the house.
includes: Siding: wood, fiber cement, aluminum, and stucco
Caulking gaps so water stays out

faq.question: When can you paint outside?
faq.answer: Usually April through October. Paint needs the right weather to stick. If it's too cold or wet, we'll tell you it's worth waiting.

faq.question: What if it rains?
faq.answer: We stop and cover things up. Rain can push back the finish date. We'll keep you in the loop.

faq.question: Do you power wash?
faq.answer: Yes. We use the right pressure for your siding, because too much can hurt old wood.

faq.question: How long will it last?
faq.answer: It depends on how much sun and weather your house gets. When we come look, we'll tell you what we see.

steps.title: Wash it
steps.body: Dirt and mildew come off first. Paint won't stick to a dirty wall.

steps.title: Scrape and sand
steps.body: Loose and peeling paint comes off. We sand the edges smooth so they don't show.

steps.title: Prime and caulk
steps.body: Bare spots get primer and gaps get caulk. This is what makes the paint last.

steps.title: Paint, and watch the sky
steps.body: Two coats. We plan around the sun and rain so the paint dries right.

stepsLede: Outside paint lasts because of the prep. Washing, scraping, and priming take the most time, and they matter the most.
